title: Matrix Orthogonalization Improves Memory in Recurrent Models
summary: This article explains how orthogonal matrices can improve memory retention in recurrent neural networks (RNNs). By using orthogonal weight initialization and parameterization, the gradients flow more stably during backpropagation through time, preventing vanishing/exploding gradients and enabling better long-term dependency learning.
problem_solved: The vanishing and exploding gradient problem that makes it difficult for recurrent models to learn long-range dependencies.
why_valuable: Orthogonal matrices provide stable gradient flow and preserve vector norms through matrix multiplications, enabling RNNs to maintain memory over long sequences without degradation.
